- **Plant part affected**: Banana leaf (midrib/central vein visible running diagonally)
- **Key visual features**:

  - Dark brown to black spots and streaks scattered across the yellowed tissue
  - No distinct pale grey concentric rings (ruling out Cordana Leaf Spot)
  - No fruit or stem involvement (ruling out Cigar End Rot, Anthracnose)
  - No narrow upright leaves with dark green streaks (ruling out Bunchy Top)
  - No pseudostem/vascular wilting (ruling out Panama Disease)

**Reasoning**: The image shows a banana leaf with extensive yellowing combined with dark black/brown spots and streaks distributed across the leaf surface. This pattern is the hallmark of **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka** — specifically Yellow Sigatoka causing chlorotic (yellow) leaf tissue with associated dark lesions. Cordana Leaf Spot is ruled out because there are no oval necrotic lesions with pale grey concentric rings or distinct yellow halos around discrete spots. The diffuse, streaky dark markings on a broadly yellowed leaf are characteristic of the Sigatoka disease complex.
